senses.gloss: whatever can be eaten raw, applied to kitchen vegetables, esp. endive &c.
units: <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 3:5">Lev. R. s. 3</cite> <he>אגודה אחת של טרוקסימא</he> (some ed. … <he>מון</he>) a bunch of vegetables.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 4:9:9">Y. Pes. IV, 31ᵇ</cite>, sq.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 7:2:23">Y. Sabb. VII, 10ᵃ</cite> <he>טריקס׳</he> ed. Krot. (corr. acc.).—

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 2:5:2">Y. Pes. II, 29ᶜ</cite> top (expl. <cite ref="P00270"><he>עולשין</he></cite>); <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 1:2:4">Y. Kil. I, 27ᵃ</cite> top (some ed. <he>מין …</he>, pl.)—

<cite ref="Tosefta Terumot 4:5">Tosef. Ter. IV, 5</cite> <he>טרקסמן</he> ed. Zuck. (Var. <he>טְרָכְסְמִין</he>, pl.) <cite ref="Tosefta Makhshirin 3:10">Tosef. Makhsh. III, 10</cite> <cite ref="I00740"><he>טרכ׳</he></cite>, contrad. to <cite ref="J00657"><he>יֶרֶק</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Berakhot 35b">Ber. 35ᵇ</cite> <he>היו … דרך ט׳ וכ׳</he> (Ms. M. <he>טרסק׳</he>; Ms. F. <he>טריבסמון</he>, corr. acc.) used to bring their fruits home (from the field to the barn) by the way of the kitchen-garden (in sight of the house) in order to make them subject to tithes; <cite ref="Gittin 81a">Gitt. 81ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 938">Yalk. Deut. 938</cite>.
